items.title: First look: Here’s what Google’s new High-visibility map style would look like
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Google Maps is working on a new High-visibility map style for navigation. 
 The option introduces a different color palette in both light and dark modes, with darker backgrounds and a purple navigation route. 
 The setting isn’t publicly available yet, but we managed to enable it in the latest version of the Google Maps Android app. 

Google Maps already gives you a few ways to customize its navigation experience. For instance, you can switch between light and dark themes and the app automatically adjusts its appearance based on your preferences or system settings. However, Google could soon give you another way to change how its maps look while navigating, and this one could make things easier to distinguish at a glance.

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

We dug into the latest Google Maps version (26.48.00.1027729593) and found an upcoming Map style setting that lets users choose between Standard and High-visibility styles. We also managed to enable the feature, giving us an early look at what the new option brings.
items.t: First look: Here’s what Google’s new High-visibility map style would look like

items.title: Google gives publishers more visibility in AI Mode with new ‘Dive Deeper’ links
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Google has started rolling out its previously announced “Dive Deeper” section in Search’s AI Mode. 
 The section displays prominent blue links, image thumbnails, and descriptions of related articles below AI-generated responses. 
 The change aims to encourage further exploration of topics while giving publishers more visibility in AI-powered search results. 

Google’s efforts to turn Search into an answer engine have left publishers fighting for clicks and some users missing the depth that traditional search results offered. While AI Mode has made researching topics less time-consuming, Google recognizes that getting a quick answer isn’t always the end of someone’s search journey. To address this, the company is now rolling out a new “Dive Deeper” section in AI Mode to encourage readers to explore articles beyond its AI-generated answers.

SEO consultant Glenn Gabe spotted and shared the change on X (via Search Engine Roundtable ). The section appears at the bottom of AI Mode responses and features prominent blue links, image thumbnails, and descriptions explaining what each article offers. It’s one of several improvements Google announced last month.
items.t: Google gives publishers more visibility in AI Mode with new ‘Dive Deeper’ links

items.title: Motorcyclists spot Google Maps on Android Auto showing routes for two-wheeled vehicles
items.summary:
Credit: KTM 

TL;DR 

Some Android Auto users report that a new motorcycle icon has appeared on Google Maps. 
 The users claim that the app has switched to motorcycle mode. 
 The app is now showing routes meant for two-wheeled vehicles, in addition to car routes. 

It’s pretty common to see reports about bugs on Android Auto. For example, users were recently having trouble with music controls . However, every now and then, you’ll come across reports about something exciting. Fortunately, today falls into the latter category, especially for those who own motorcycles.

Android Auto tends to be a car-centric experience. When using Google Maps on Android Auto, the platform normally defaults to car routes. That is true whether you’re driving in a car or some other type of vehicle. That’s why some users were taken by surprise when Google Maps on Android Auto began showing routes meant for two-wheeled vehicles.

Google is working on introducing new filters to help you sift through your Chrome history, and these go way more granular than you might have expected. The browser could soon get three new history search filters, and one of them could even let you swap between websites you visited yourself and those that were accessed by Gemini.

The development was spotted and highlighted by X user @Leopeva64 , who even shared screenshots of the redesigned history section with the new filters visible. According to the browser tipster, the new filters are already available in the Dev and Canary versions of Chrome, suggesting that they could likely go stable sometime soon.

Google is expanding 1080p video sending to all Meet users on the web.

Google Meet recently made it easier for presenters to share files with participants through direct download support . It’s a quality-of-life addition that, while not necessary, is very nice to have. Continuing on that trend, Google is now expanding full HD video sending to more users.

While Google Meet offers 1080p video sending on the web, the feature was limited to select paid users. The important word there is “was,” as that is no longer the case. Google has announced that it is now expanding access to 1080p video sending on the web to all Meet users.

From smartwatches that remember what you just said to tiny recorders that take meeting notes , companies are finding new ways to make conversations useful long after they’ve ended. Nothing has been teasing its own entry into this crowded space, and we now have our clearest picture yet of what it’s bringing to the table.

items.title: Fitbit Air gets unofficial call and notification alerts on Android and iOS
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Two unofficial apps bring notification and incoming call vibrations to the Fitbit Air. 
 Cuff offers customizable alerts on Android, while AirBuzz uses iOS 27’s Shortcuts automations. 
 Google doesn’t officially support either workaround, but both are available to try. 

Google designed the Fitbit Air for people who want to track their health without another screen competing for their attention. That philosophy explains why the band doesn’t display notifications or even vibrate when calls and messages arrive. But there’s a difference between avoiding constant distractions and wanting to know when something important needs your attention. Google hasn’t offered users that middle ground, so independent developers have stepped in.

Two unofficial apps, Cuff for Android and AirBuzz for iOS, let the Fitbit Air buzz for incoming calls and notifications, giving owners a choice Google left out. As shared on Reddit (via Android Police ), Cuff reverse-engineers the tracker’s Bluetooth communication, letting users choose which alerts reach their wrists and customize how the band vibrates.
items.t: Fitbit Air gets unofficial call and notification alerts on Android and iOS

items.title: Gemini for Home is winning praise from new users as opinions begin to shift
items.summary:

The migration from Google Assistant to Gemini for Home that started a little over a year ago has been met mostly with grievances, but occasionally there is a report from a satisfied user or two — and based on what we’re seeing in the Google Home sub on Reddit , we might start hearing more of these positive vibes.

Our poster notes that they had resisted updating their Google Nest Mini but finally gave in to get rid of the notifications about Gemini. They were ready for it to go badly, yet ended up impressed with things like how quickly Gemini responds to commands to turn lights on and off. “I thought it was going to be horrible so I did plan to set up a new home to switch back to Google assistant just in case,” they wrote. “But Gemini turned out to be great.”

items.title: YouTube introduces a new mute button on mobile, but not everyone is happy
items.summary:
TL;DR 

YouTube is rolling out a dedicated mute button within its mobile video player, letting users silence videos without adjusting their device’s volume. 
 Some users are frustrated by the button’s placement, reporting accidental presses when trying to skip forward in videos. 
 The feature appears to be rolling out gradually. We have it on iOS, but not on Android. 

YouTube is finally giving users on its mobile apps an easier way to outright silence video without having to fiddle with their device’s volume controls, and it’s manifesting in the form of a dedicated mute button . Although the new button does sound like a welcome addition, many users are already finding the change frustrating , mainly because of accidental presses.

The quality-of-life change doesn’t appear to be entirely new. We found a Reddit post from early October highlighting the mute button, suggesting that the streaming giant has been experimenting with it since then, at the very least. However, more recent reports indicate that the button is now making its way to a lot more users simultaneously (thanks @GreenShades9 ).
items.t: YouTube introduces a new mute button on mobile, but not everyone is happy

items.title: Amazon is ending software support for the 10th-gen Kindle and Paperwhite
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Amazon is ending software support for the 10th-generation Kindle and Kindle Paperwhite. 
 Both e-readers should continue working normally, with access to downloaded books and the Kindle Store remaining unaffected for now. 
 Amazon previously discontinued Kindle Store support for devices released in 2012 or earlier, but there’s no confirmed cutoff date for these newer models. 

One of the best things about owning a Kindle is that you don’t have to replace it every few years. As long as the screen works and the battery holds up, even an older model can serve you well. Unfortunately, if you’re still using a 10th-generation Kindle or Kindle Paperwhite, there’s some disappointing news.

As first spotted by Good e-Reader , Amazon is ending software support for both e-readers . The 10th-generation Kindle, released in April 2019, and the Kindle Paperwhite, which arrived in November 2018, will no longer receive software updates, including security patches.
items.t: Amazon is ending software support for the 10th-gen Kindle and Paperwhite

Live notifications on Galaxy devices are part of the Now Bar and offer continuous updates from supported apps directly on the status bar. items.title: Xiaomi 19 series rumored to get a much wider ultrawide camera
items.summary:
Xiaomi took the Xiaomi 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max global last week, but the rumor mill has already moved on to the Xiaomi 19 series. Today, Digital Chat Station on Weibo is claiming that the phones coming in 2027 should get a "true" ultrawide camera. According to him, the 50MP OmniVision OV51C sensor will be used, paired with a roughly 14mm lens and a field of view of around 114°.

This would be a very welcome development for Xiaomi, since its ultrawides aren't exactly known for being very wide. Case in point: the Xiaomi 18 Pro has a 50MP 1/2.87" ultrawide with a 17mm lens and a 102° field of...
items.t: Xiaomi 19 series rumored to get a much wider ultrawide camera

items.title: Apple will focus on affordable models in early 2027 - iPhone 18e, new iPad, new MacBook Neo
items.summary:
When he took over the CEO position, John Ternus said that he wants Apple to move away from the traditional big September announcement and to launch new products more often. We’re already seeing that – the September iPhone event only brought the two iPhone 18 Pro models and Apple’s first foldable. The remaining iPhone models will come next year.

It will start with the iPhone 18e in the February-March time frame, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman. This is when Apple is expected to release iOS 27.4. The “.4” releases tend to be a major milestone in the iOS release cycle – any features that...
items.t: Apple will focus on affordable models in early 2027 - iPhone 18e, new iPad, new MacBook Neo

items.title: MacBook trackpads can now talk in a robot voice without the speakers, thanks to a free tool
items.summary: Nospeaker is a free open-source tool that drives a MacBook's Force Touch haptic motor up to 4,000 times a second so the trackpad can speak text you type. It is quieter on your lap and has only been tested on one Mac.
items.t: MacBook trackpads can now talk in a robot voice without the speakers, thanks to a free tool

items.title: Honor 700 and 700S arrive with rear screens, 200MP cameras and 9,000mAh batteries
items.summary:
The Honor 700 series is now official in China with three members, and we’ll be taking a closer look at the Honor 700 and 700S in the following lines. The standout feature for this year is the rear screen, which is present on all three phones.

items.title: Honor 700 Pro debuts with a Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 SoC and a 9,000mAh battery
items.summary:
Honor's latest number series has officially debuted in China, comprising the Honor 700, 700 Pro, and 700S. All three phones feature a rear screen and a 6.57-inch main display, while the Pro model gets a few additional upgrades.

The Honor 700 Pro is powered by the Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 chipset, paired with the Adreno 829 GPU, up to 16GB of RAM, and up to 512GB of storage.

At the front, the phone features a 6.57-inch AMOLED display with 1.5K resolution, a 120Hz refresh rate, and up to 8,000 nits of peak brightness. It also gets a 1.59-inch AMOLED display on the rear.

items.t: Honor 700 Pro debuts with a Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 SoC and a 9,000mAh battery

items.title: iPhone Duo may soon support more widgets on its Lock Screen
items.summary:
The iPhone Duo currently supports two customizable shortcuts on its lock screen, positioned in the bottom-right corner. However, a tipster claims Apple has been testing new Lock Screen widgets for the foldable, which could arrive in a future software update.

Leakster pdfu shared the findings on X, along with a video showing the new widgets in action. According to the tipster, Apple tested a new “complication column” that can accommodate two widgets.

The widget box will appear below the network status indicators on the right side of the cover screen. It was first spotted in iOS 27.1,...
items.t: iPhone Duo may soon support more widgets on its Lock Screen

items.title: Google is killing off the Nest app and Google Assistant on Home devices
items.summary:
In traditional Google fashion, the online titan just can’t seem to make up its mind on what is mostly semantics and end-user marketing matters. A couple of changes were recently announced for 2027, pertaining to Google Home devices.

First up, the Nest app for Android, iOS and the web version will all be shutting down on January 25, 2027. If you are still using that for one reason or another to manage some Nest devices, you need to move over to the Google Home app. The switch is mostly handled on the backend by Google. They will migrate all your devices, including cameras and their...
items.t: Google is killing off the Nest app and Google Assistant on Home devices

items.title: Samsung may shift Galaxy Watch to a two-year launch cycle
items.summary:
According to a new report from South Korea, Samsung may skip launching a new Galaxy Watch lineup next year and shift to a two-year release cycle. The company has followed an annual launch schedule since introducing the first Galaxy Watch in 2018.

The report, citing industry sources, claims that Samsung Electronics' Mobile eXperience (MX) division has reportedly been facing losses for the past two quarters, prompting the company to consider structural changes to improve profitability.

items.t: Samsung may shift Galaxy Watch to a two-year launch cycle

items.title: Xiaomi 18 Pro series goes global, anniversary iPhone details surface, Week 47 in review
items.summary:
This week's most popular article isn't about phones, it's about Instagram. It seems like the latest Instagram update got people's attention and introduced a feature that people have been waiting for for years - the ability to edit stories after posting them. You can change text, music, stickers, and drawings. Of course, there's a catch. You can edit stories only 15 minutes after posting them.

items.title: The rumored vivo I2606 is powered by the Snapdragon 8s Gen 4
items.summary:
A few days ago, we saw a BIS certification listing for the vivo I2606. Since we already know the iQOO 16 family is coming to the country, likely at an unfortunately high price, we just put two and two together.

vivo I2606 on GeekBench and BIS

Well, now we have a GeekBench score from the I2606, proving that it is running the Snapdragon 8s Gen 4 (SM8735), along with 12GB of RAM and Android 17.
